items.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: one of my friends who I was staying with, Tony Keller, who was the director of the Commission on the Arts

ctx.x: That’s where they started me on that. I went around and met Cheryl Smith, the lady you met yesterday, and a few other people, and Dollie and I. We started meeting. We started talking about – well, that’s later on. First I started meeting some people and commuting back and forth. So I looked up, and I was here four days a week. I finally said to Dollie – I said, “You know, I wouldn’t mind moving out of here,” because we had a beautiful apartment on Avenue C and 13th Street. We lived at 1 Haven Plaza. We were up on…

have that here.” She said, “No, I don’t want to live up here. This is tired.” So she went back to New York, and I was still commuting back and forth. Then I came home one – I used to come home on Thursday night and stay Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, and leave Monday, come back up here. I said, “Dollie, I’m going to look at a house.” I said, “And once I look at this house, if I like it, will you come up and look at the house with me? Just look at the house.” So she said, oh man.
